episodes.title: Reinventing School for the AI Era | Joe Liemandt, Gagan Biyani & Erik Torenberg
episodes.about: What should school look like if AI can help students learn dramatically faster? Alpha School founder Joe Liemandt argues the answer is not to fill the extra time with more academics, but to redesign school around the skills traditional classrooms struggle to teach: agency, teamwork, entrepreneurship, communication, and doing hard things. Joe joins Erik Torenberg and Horowitz and Andreessen Academy co-founder Gagan Biyani to discuss Alpha's model, where students spend two hours a day on core academics with AI help and the rest on those harder-to-teach skills.
episodes.why: Out today: Alpha School's Joe Liemandt argues AI lets students finish core academics in two hours, so school should be redesigned around agency, teamwork and doing hard things.

episodes.title: 4 Questions for AI This Week
episodes.about: Is China closing the AI gap? Is cyber chaos the new normal? Is data center funding drying up? And what happens if Anthropic's IPO disappoints? From Kimi K3.1 to rogue agent swarms to Elon Musk's debt market warning, NLW examines the four questions shaping AI this week.
episodes.why: Kimi K3.1, rogue agent swarms and a possible China gap: NLW frames the four questions shaping AI this week, including whether cyber chaos is the new normal.

episodes.title: When AI agents run your life
episodes.about: What you gain, and what you give up, when you let AI agents take control. This episode was produced by Kelli Wessinger, edited by Avishay Artsy, fact-checked by Melissa Hirsch, engineered by Bridger Dunnagan, and hosted by Jonquilyn Hill.
episodes.why: Vox asks what you gain, and what you give up, when you let AI agents take control of daily life.

episodes.title: Mathematics Just Changed Forever — Kevin Hartnett
episodes.about: Kevin Hartnett is the author of The Proof in the Code. In 1998 Thomas Hales finished a proof of the Kepler conjecture that leaned so heavily on computer code that the Annals of Mathematics could not say whether it was true. That impasse opens Hartnett's book The Proof in the Code, and this documentary-style conversation about computer-checked proofs, the Lean proof assistant, and how machine verification is changing what mathematicians can trust.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Machine Learning Street Talk is a long-form machine-learning interview show, new here: Kevin Hartnett traces how computer-checked proofs, from the Kepler conjecture to Lean, are changing what counts as mathematical truth.

episodes.title: Why Digital Price Tags Are Spooking Shoppers
episodes.about: American shoppers are worried that businesses are using artificial intelligence and other tech to inflate prices. WSJ retail reporter Sarah Nassauer says that is driven by data privacy concerns, rising costs of living, and AI anxiety. But is it actually becoming more common? Danny Lewis hosts.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — WSJ Tech News Briefing is the Journal's short daily tech show, new here: shoppers fear AI is quietly inflating prices with digital price tags, and WSJ checks whether it is actually happening.
